Admissions Requirements
Doctor of Philosophy
Doctor of Philosophy
Application Materials
Statement of Purpose: 500–1,000 words (the admissions application displays a 500 word limit but accepts higher word counts).
Three letters of recommendation
Unofficial transcripts
Resumé or Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Every institution of higher education attended;
All previous employment since the applicant’s 18th birthday;
A list of published materials and significant research, writing, or editorial contributions;
Current and pending research funding from any source, including the funder, amount, applicant’s role, and a brief description of the research; and
A full disclosure of non-university professional activities, including any affiliation with an institution or program in a foreign country.
International Applicants: English Language Proficiency Exam (see exemptions)
Not Required: Graduate Record Examination (GRE)
Not Required: Fundamentals of Engineering Examination (FE)
Minimum Requirements
Funding verification is an admission requirement for the MAE PhD program. (See funding options)
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Math, Physics, or Statistics
Upper-Division Undergraduate (Worksheet) or Graduate GPA above 3.0
International Applicants: IELTS(6.5+) or TOEFL (4.5+ overall, with 4.0+ in each subsection)

Master of Science
Application Materials
Statement of Purpose, 500 words or less
Two letters of recommendation
Unofficial transcripts
Resumé
International Applicants: English Language Proficiency Exam (see exemptions)
Not Required: Graduate Record Examination (GRE)
Not Required: Fundamentals of Engineering Examination (FE)

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Math, Physics, or Statistics
Upper-Division GPA above 3.0 (worksheet)
International Applicants: IELTS(6.5+) or TOEFL (4.5+ overall, with 4.0+ in each subsection)

Certificate
Minimum Requirements

OR

Not Required: Graduate Record Examination (GRE)
Not Required: Fundamentals of Engineering Examination (FE)
Post-Baccalaureate
Post-Baccalaureate
Why Post-Baccalaureate?
MAE Post-Baccalaureate is a non-degree enrollment option for students who wish to establish or improve their graduate GPA, to become a stronger candidate for future graduate studies. Students may take up to three engineering graduate classes, with online options available, which may be eligible for transfer to an MAE graduate degree.
Post-Baccalaureate students are not permitted to take undergraduate coursework.
Suggested Preparatory Undergraduate Coursework or Fundamental Knowledge:
Calculus 1-3
Differential Equations
Physics 1-2
For those interested in…
Structure/Manufacturing, take Statics and Mechanics courses
Aerodynamics, take Thermodynamics, Fluids, Heat Transfer courses
Guidance and Control, take Statics, Dynamics, and Controls courses
